title: Platform tenant ownership and operator autonomy playbook
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary

This playbook defines how platform teams at Redwood assign tenant-level ownership, empower operators with safe autonomy, and avoid costly manual coordination during incidents or routine adjustments. It provides concrete ownership boundaries, operator runbook patterns, automation primitives, and an escalation matrix tailored for multi-tenant LLM inference workloads.

Intended audience
- Platform operators and oncall engineers
- Service owners (allocator, batch-router, kv-prefix-cache, telemetry-gateway)
- SRE leads and platform product managers

Goals
- Make it explicit who owns tenant-level behaviors and cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Reduce manual cross-team handoffs for routine tenant actions by 60% in Q3 2025.
- Provide operator primitives and safety checks that allow trusted operators to take temporary, reversible actions without engineering tickets.

Key definitions
- Tenant: a billing/identity boundary (customer or internal team) consuming inference capacity.
- Tenant owner: product or internal team responsible for feature correctness and business impact.
- Platform operator: oncall engineer operating platform runtime (allocator, cache, router).
- Operator autonomy: set of pre-approved actions an operator can take without additional approvals.

Ownership boundaries (decision matrix)
| Area | Primary owner | Operator-level actions allowed | Notes |
|------|---------------|-------------------------------|-------|
| Model variants, config (quantization, seq-limits) | Model-ops / Applied ML | Suggest model variant via admin API; cannot change production pin | Operators may toggle non-production pins for staging only.
| Tenant capacity & quota | Platform SRE (operational), Product/Finance (billing) | Temp burst credits, soft-throttle, emergency eviction (see runbook) | All changes must be recorded and auto-reverted when expiry hits.
| Prefetch & kv-prefix-cache | Platform runtime team | Restart prefetch jobs, mark tenant prefetch suspended | Suspension limited to 60 minutes unless owner consent.
| Request routing policy | Platform routing team | Move tenant to regional fallback pool under approved runbook | Movement must preserve PII-region constraints.
| Telemetry/alert thresholds | Platform observability team | Silence low-priority alerts for 1-hour windows | Silences must include reason and owners.

Operator autonomy catalog (approved primitives)
- grant-burst-credit tenant=<id> duration=30m amount=50k-tokens -- transient; audited
- suspend-prefetch tenant=<id> duration=60m -- causes reduced cache hit rate but reduces memory pressure
- move-tenant-pool tenant=<id> pool=regional-fallback -- only for latency-constrained emergency; respects data residency tags
- emergency-evict tenant=<id> reason=<short> -- evict from shared pools to isolated capacity; requires operator checklist

Operator checklist for emergency-evict (must be run in order)
1. Notify tenant owner via PagerDuty if contact exists; if not, create internal ticket and assign to Platform SRE.
2. Record justification and expected impact in action log (CLI: platform-ops log-action ...).
3. run: platform-ops emergency-evict --tenant <id> --duration 2h --dry-run=false
4. Confirm traffic drain metrics: inflight_tokens < 1000 and active_streams == 0 for 120s.
5. Monitor SLOs for adjacent tenants for 15 minutes.
6. If adverse effects observed, run rollback: platform-ops emergency-un-evict --tenant <id>

Automation and guardrails
- All operator primitives are implemented as idempotent API endpoints behind RBAC. Only roles: operator, operator-senior, platform-admin are mapped to CLI tokens.
- Time-bound changes auto-revert via scheduler (default TTL = 2 hours).
- Every change emits a structured audit event to telemetry-gateway.audit with fields: actor, action, tenant_id, reason, expiry_ts. Example JSON (stored as string in event):
{ 
  "actor": "oncall:maya",
  "action": "grant-burst-credit",
  "tenant_id": "tr-12345",
  "amount": "50k-tokens",
  "expiry_ts": "2025-09-01T12:34:56Z"
}
- Safe-mode policy: if >3 operator actions touch the same tenant in 24h, further operator-only changes are blocked and owner notification escalates to product.

Runbooks (short)
A. Tenant degraded (high tail latency)
1. Check per-tenant SLOs: query dashboard 'tenant-slo-summary' for tenant id.
2. Inspect cache hit rate: telemetry-gateway.query metric=kv_prefix_cache.hit_rate tenant=<id>.
3. If hit_rate < 20% and memory pressure high: suspend-prefetch for tenant for 60m.
4. If CPU or GPU scheduling delayed (queue depth > 200): grant-burst-credit for 30m and move-tenant-pool to regional-fallback.
5. Continue to monitor for 30 minutes, if no improvement, escalate to model-ops for model variant rollback.

B. Cost surge (unexpected token burn)
1. Identify spike via cost-attribution dashboard and tokenized trace.
2. If spike source = single tenant and >50% of delta, run temporary soft-throttle: platform-ops set-rate-limit tenant=<id> rps=10 for 1h.
3. Notify billing/product and create long-term review ticket.

Escalation matrix
- Operator detects cross-tenant impact: page Platform SRE lead (P1) and create incident channel.
- Tenant owner reachable: platform operator coordinates remediation directly with owner (no ticket required for transient changes).
- Tenant owner unreachable: platform operator may take emergency-evict and must create ticket within 30 minutes.

Operational dashboards and alerts guidance
- Minimum dashboards to maintain per tenant: SLO (p95 latency), token-rate, active_streams, kv_cache_hit_rate, queue_depth, recent-operator-actions.
- Alert thresholds (example):
  - p95 latency > 1.5x SLO for 5m => severity P2 (notify operator).
  - token-rate spike > 3x rolling-5m baseline => P1 (notify oncall and billing).
  - kv_cache_hit_rate < 15% for 10m with memory_usage > 80% => P1.
- Alert action cards should include: probable cause, quick runbook link, one-click actions (suspend-prefetch, grant-burst-credit) where safe.

Tooling snippets and examples
- Grant burst credit (CLI)
$ platform-ops grant-burst-credit --tenant tr-12345 --amount 50000 --duration 30m --reason "regional latency mitigation"

- Suspend prefetch (curl)
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/api/v1/tenants/tr-12345/prefetch/suspend \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN' \n  -d '{"duration":"60m","reason":"memory pressure"}'

- Audit query (sql-like)
SELECT actor, action, tenant_id, ts FROM telemetry_gateway.audit WHERE tenant_id='tr-12345' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 100;

Rollout and training plan
- Q2 2025: Ship RBAC-backed operator primitives to staging and train oncall cohort via 2 gamedays.
- Q3 2025: Gradual roll to production for operators with >3 months oncall experience; policy TTL defaults enabled.
- Continuous: monthly retro on operator actions logged to identify policy gaps.

Metrics for success (OKRs)
- Reduce cross-team ticket count for tenant-operational actions by 60% by end of Q3 2025.
- Mean time to remediate tenant latency incidents (operator-resolved) < 20 minutes.
- No customer-facing data residency violations from operator actions (zero tolerance).

Retrospective triggers
- Any emergency-evict that results in cascading degradation to >2 tenants triggers a post-incident retro and ownership review.
- If >5 operator audits are missing justification in a quarter, retrain operators and tighten RBAC.

Appendix: quick reference matrix
- Allowed direct operator actions: suspend-prefetch, grant-burst-credit, set-rate-limit (soft), move-tenant-pool (fallback), emergency-evict
- Actions requiring owner consent: model pin changes; persistent quota increases; changes to data residency
